chunks: From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'What is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That she answers his call to intimacy, even if she is on a camel's hump (from fatigue or position), and does not give anything (of her body or self) except with his permission. If she does so, the burden (of disobedience) is upon her and the reward is for him. And that she does not spend a night while he is angry with her.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he is unjust?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Yes.' She said, 'By the One Who sent you with the Truth, I will never marry a husband!'

key_terms.قَتَبٍ: Camel's hump (idiom for difficulty or position)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a husband upon his wife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational marital duties in Shia jurisprudence, particularly emphasizing 'ans al-hajah' (sexual compliance) as a primary right, even if the wife is physically indisposed ('ala qatb'), while linking obedience to divine reward and sin. The narrative highlights the concept of 'sukhṭ' (anger/displeasure) as a marital disruption to be avoided, underscoring the importance of emotional harmony alongside physical duties. The woman’s exclamation reflects the weight of these obligations, illustrating the reciprocal nature of rights and duties within the Islamic marital contract.
